claims: C1 the assistant must strive to follow all applicable instructions when producing a response
C2 system, developer and user instructions are included among the instructions to follow
C3 an instruction that conflicts with a higher-authority instruction is excepted from the duty to follow
C4 an instruction that conflicts with a later instruction at the same authority is excepted from the duty to follow

concepts.name: applicable_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that applies to the current request, determined by filtering candidate instructions
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: system_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the system authority level
concepts.inference: the clause names system, developer and user instructions as the classes included; each class needs a predicate to range over

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the developer authority level
concepts.inference: the clause names system, developer and user instructions as the classes included; each class needs a predicate to range over

concepts.name: user_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the user authority level
concepts.inference: the clause names system, developer and user instructions as the classes included; each class needs a predicate to range over

concepts.name: instruction_authority
concepts.gloss: instruction I is issued at authority level L
concepts.inference: comparing authority between instructions requires each instruction to carry an authority level

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: instruction I conflicts with instruction J, meaning following both would be inconsistent
concepts.inference: the exception is defined by conflict between instructions; which pairs conflict is a fact about the case

concepts.name: later_instruction
concepts.gloss: instruction I is later in the conversation than instruction J
concepts.inference: the same-authority exception is defined by one instruction being later than another; which order holds is a fact about the case

concepts.name: excepted_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that is excepted from the duty to follow because it conflicts with a higher-authority instruction or a later instruction at the same authority
concepts.inference: the clause defines two exception conditions; a single predicate collects them so the obligation can refer to the exception

ontology.gloss: I is excepted because it conflicts with a higher-authority instruction
ontology.body: conflicts_with(I, J), instruction_authority(I, L1), instruction_authority(J, L2), authority_levels_hierarchy(L2, L1)

ontology.gloss: I is excepted because it conflicts with a later instruction at the same authority
ontology.body: conflicts_with(I, J), instruction_authority(I, L), instruction_authority(J, L), later_instruction(J, I)

asserts.read_back: following instruction % is obliged because it is an applicable instruction and not excepted

closure.reason: the clause obliges following applicable instructions and carves out only the two stated conflict exceptions; an instruction that is not applicable is outside the duty, and silence about non-applicable instructions leaves them permitted
